clue.text: Spooner's accused principal dancer of being a promiscuous type

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words this phrase yields trade places

blocks.note: a principal is a head, and a bopper is someone dancing to pop; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A head dancer of a company is accused by Spooner of sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAD BOPPER with its opening sounds swapped becomes BED HOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hops from one bed to another is a person with many casual sexual partners.

clue.text: Constable is a bit soft, having released Liberal

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: blobby means soft and shapeless
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A police constable is accused of being rather soft after letting a Liberal go.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOBBY loses its L to leave BOBBY; a bobby is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is an informal British name for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel, founder of the force.

clue.text: Made call to get cops involved in action

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is caught up inside it

blocks.note: first part of DEED, an action
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
rest of DEED, an action

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to bring the police in on a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: CID sits inside DEED. The CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to make a call, in the sense of reaching a judgement on something.

clue.text: It was used to make Roman omelette

definitions.text: It was used to make Roman omelette

blocks.clueFragment: It was used to make Roman omelette
blocks.note: surface reading: an ingredient or pan used in cooking in ancient Rome
setter's reading: the Latin word for the egg in an omelette

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' points to Latin, not Italian cookery; the word is the Latin for egg, now also the biological term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the word means an egg, the essential ingredient of any omelette.

clue.text: Look briefly at reports of maximum irritation

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: maximum is a peak; irritation is pique, which sounds the same too

explanation.surface: Someone glances at news of how annoyed people have become.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'maximum' (peak) and 'irritation' (pique) sound like the answer, so the clue offers two routes to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick glance, a brief or furtive look.

clue.text: Experience of getting high yield before – it's coming back

blocks.note: a return is the yield on an investment
a trip is a drug experience

explanation.surface: Someone recalls getting high and a big pay-out, and expects it to recur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts the yield word ahead of the drug experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A return trip is the homeward leg of a journey, the part where you come back.

clue.text: Important religious text is sectarian

blocks.note: big means important
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A major scripture is accused of being divisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectarian, as a noun, is a narrow-minded zealot for one group, which is what a bigot is.

clue.text: Pay-off at end of poem

blocks.note: first meaning: the final result or what really matters
second meaning: literally the last line on the page

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: the lowest line of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the final outcome or profit figure, and literally names the last line of any text.

clue.text: Island got really enraged initially over nothing

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: first letters of three words
nada is Spanish for nothing, used in English slang

explanation.surface: Someone got furious on the island over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the initials above the word for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation in the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Seem awkward wearing underwear for introduction to programme

indicators.note: something awkward is out of sorts, so the letters are rearranged
underwear wearing something has it on the inside, so it goes within

blocks.note: first part of THONG, a skimpy item of underwear
letters of the word rearranged
rest of THONG

explanation.surface: Wearing a thong seems awkward to open a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'Seem' go inside THONG after its TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the tune played at the start of a TV or radio programme.

clue.text: Melting ice sheet's a brute – why climb it?

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber faces a fearsome ice sheet and wonders why they bother.
explanation.walkthrough: George Mallory's famous reply when asked why he wanted to climb Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the classic mountaineer's answer to the question of why one would climb a peak.

clue.text: My good man – regularly forceful he is

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a friend, remarking in odd word order that he is strong-willed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is phrased in the Jedi master's own back-to-front speech; 'forceful' means strong in the Force of Star Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoda is the Star Wars Jedi master, deeply attuned to the Force and famed for inverted sentences.

clue.text: Appropriate entrance for central Harrow?

indicators.note: central means the middle part, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: the inner four letters
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone asks what would be a fitting gateway into the middle of Harrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (fitting) but is the verb, to seize. Harrow is a London district with a famous school.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize something without right, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: They'll see you in court for covering street with obstacles

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping round it, so it sits within

blocks.note: first part of BARRIERS, obstacles
ST is the abbreviation for street
rest of BARRIERS

explanation.surface: Lawyers will see you in court for blocking off a road with barricades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see you' suggests a threat; it is the lawyers who meet clients there.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers are the lawyers who argue cases in court, representing clients there.

clue.text: Omit cover for privates providing order in sticky situation

blocks.note: first meaning: wear no underwear
second meaning: a command telling a special-forces soldier to move

explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' looks military, matching the commando theme, but means private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to wear no underpants, and read literally is a command to a commando soldier.

clue.text: Normal lady at home opposes such a loner

indicators.note: opposes asks for the opposite of each word before them, which are then strung together

blocks.note: odd is the opposite of normal
man is the opposite of lady
out is the opposite of in, at home

explanation.surface: An ordinary woman who stays in objects to such an isolated person.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words or phrases is swapped for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd man out is the one who does not fit with the rest of a group, a loner.

clue.text: Seafood store where ragged boy rested

indicators.note: ragged means torn and untidy, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop selling seafood where a scruffy lad took a break.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is a place on the seabed where oysters are bred or grow, a natural larder.

clue.text: Plain part of Cornwall an oasis

indicators.note: part of tells you the answer is a section of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and on through the next two

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Cornwall, a flat area is a welcome refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in the far south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain, especially in Spanish America.

clue.text: Your drained, after having modelled for this randy fellow

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: a model sits for an artist
first and last letters

explanation.surface: An artist's model is worn out after posing for a lecherous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the emptied word behind the posing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful woodland god of Greek myth, and by extension a lecherous man.

clue.text: He recorded his times without telling us

blocks.note: tacit means unspoken, understood without being said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chronicler wrote down events without letting us know.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman historian who wrote the Annals and Histories of his own era.

clue.text: No ironing when drunk! Get some food

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers, so these letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice not to do the household chores while drunk, but to grab a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion ring is a battered, deep-fried slice of onion served as a side dish.

clue.text: Authoritative reason given to child querying parental order

definitions.text: Authoritative reason given to child querying parental order

blocks.note: surface reading: a sound, well-argued justification
setter's reading: the parent's stock reply to 'Why?', which rests only on authority

explanation.walkthrough: 'Authoritative' is ironic: the reason is nothing but the parent's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents answer a child's 'Why should I?' with this phrase, offering their word as the only justification.

clue.text: Let me through for this dance

blocks.note: first meaning: a polite request to pass
second meaning: a ballroom dance in which partners may be claimed by others

explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is a dance where a person may cut in on a couple, so the two senses meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite request to get past, and also names a dance in which partners can be taken over.

clue.text: Asian money needed when adding height to club …

indicators.note: adding a letter into a word here means slipping it inside

blocks.note: first part of BAT, a club
H is the abbreviation for height
rest of BAT

explanation.surface: Someone needs cash to make a club taller, and the clue runs on into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 25, but the two are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency of Thailand, in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Stand over major city – just a bit

blocks.note: a golf tee is a stand for the ball
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Someone stands above a great city, barely visible.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the stand on top of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny means very small, a tiny amount, which is just a bit.

clue.text: Make mistake and scarper without finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: to go off is to run away

explanation.surface: Someone blunders and then bolts before the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To goof is to make a silly blunder, an informal word for an error.

clue.text: Spirit shown by master catholic

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts
RC is Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Catholic headmaster displays great fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins and pips left after winemaking.

clue.text: … our central location for revealing secrets

blocks.note: first meaning: literally the place in the middle of two people
second meaning: the phrase that prefaces a confidence

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 21 for the surface only; read alone, 'our central location' is the space between us.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces something said in confidence, and literally places a thing in the middle of the two of us.

clue.text: Drug measures would be heartless for some females

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle taken out, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: does are female deer or rabbits

explanation.surface: Drug doses would be cruel for some women.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer with its central S removed leaves DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured quantities of a medicine taken at one time.

clue.text: Faded plant lacks depth on the nose

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: faded things are old and worn
D is the abbreviation for depth
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A wilted plant without depth still has some fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks botanical but is industrial; OLD loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfactory means relating to the sense of smell, which is centred on the nose.
